sections.title: Identification and form
sections.text: The catalogue entry represents Papaver rhoeas, the common poppy, not the opium poppy. This annual is usually 30–60 cm tall and grows in fields and disturbed soils.

sections.title: Flowers and fruit
sections.text: The flower has four red petals. The latex is whitish. The short capsule has a radiating stigmatic disc and opens through pores beneath the disc.

sections.title: Uses and toxicity
sections.text: The petals are traditionally used in infusions. INRAE reports a toxic risk, especially associated with the fruit; poisoning has been reported after eating buds. Do not treat the whole plant as edible or confuse its seeds with food poppy seeds.
